original_test_intent: Interrupt a valid firmware upgrade at the approved in-progress stage and verify ERoT/Aps atomic recovery retains the previous firmware and returns the SUT to a normal OS after controlled power restoration.
original_method: Use a dedicated sacrificial SUT; identify exact component, current/target banks and valid signed image; preserve baseline and prove recovery route; start vendor-approved update with observable stage; operator removes power only at documented injection point; record outage/dwell/restore; inspect ERoT/Aps state, task/journal and active/staged versions; boot OS and verify GPU/baseboard/management/log health; no retry.
manual_activity: Firmware owner defines component/image/stage/atomicity; operator physically controls power on a recovery-ready system and owns vendor recovery; agent prepares, observes and verifies only.
required_inputs: Exact ERoT/Aps target, active/staged bank and current/target versions
Valid signed update image/hash and update mechanism
Vendor-approved observable interruption stage, acceptable timing and power-off dwell
Dedicated SUT, recovery image/tool, console/OOB/PDU and maintenance approval
safety_requirements: Never improvise an interruption point or use production hardware
Agent must not unplug or restore power
Abort before injection if stage visibility or recovery path is uncertain
Preserve all partial-update and power evidence
No reflash, retry or forced recovery without explicit engineer ownership
agent_execution_scope: Prepare update and timestamp observable state for operator action
engineer_actions: Resolve ERoT/Aps scope and approve fault point/oracle
Authorize operator power action and own recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Corrupt/tampered images test validation rejection, not power-loss atomicity; only a valid approved update at a defined stage covers this row.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Start the exact signed update, expose the vendor-defined in-progress checkpoint, have the operator interrupt/restore power at that point, then read atomicity state and previous active version before normal boot validation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Physical power-cord interruption and previous-version recovery are preserved; timing and component are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Synchronize update-stage telemetry, independent PDU event timestamps and firmware-bank/journal evidence so the injected failure is reproducible and attributable.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns an unbounded unplug instruction into a precisely gated fault-injection transaction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Invalid-image rejection does not exercise persistence while a valid image is being written.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: This is deliberately destructive; even expected rollback can fail and require board-level vendor recovery.

project_override_considerations: Security firmware owner defines ERoT/Aps bank/journal semantics and which write stage may be interrupted without exceeding lab safety policy.
expected_evidence: Target/bank/current-target version and valid signed image hash
Previous firmware proof, BMC/console and OS boot
GPU/baseboard/driver/management plus SEL/dmesg health and recovery disposition

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row names ERoT and Aps but gives no exact component or firmware-bank target, and 'when updating' does not define the required interruption phase, duration or atomic recovery state.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; the hazardous execution remains gated by vendor and operator decisions.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row272 Wistron-NV GPU-00265-V002: identify ERoT/Aps target and active/staged banks, valid signed image/current-target versions, the exact observable vendor-approved interruption stage and power-off dwell, expected journal/rollback state, and dedicated-SUT recovery path. Do not substitute row271 invalid images.

review_improvement: Defines a controlled, observable power-loss fault injection and proves atomic prior-version recovery across firmware, boot and platform health.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power removal before validation, during staging, during bank switch and after commit exercise different atomicity guarantees. Without a stage marker, a successful old-version boot may mean the update never began rather than resilience. Independent power timestamps and firmware journal/bank evidence establish that interruption occurred at the intended point, while full OS/device health detects partial recovery that a version string alone misses.
